Hannah,

Thanks for circling back. Per our internal counsel, Valora needs a clear carve-out to the liability cap where there is unauthorized acquisition or misappropriation of trade secrets or other highly sensitive IP. The sticking point for us is (i) how Redwood defines a "trade secret" event, and (ii) what neutral evidence or thresholds justify elevating damages beyond the standard cap.

To make progress, can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: 
- accept a narrowly tailored carve-out for proven trade-secret misappropriation (not just alleged leaks), and
- include an evidence/forensics protocol that specifies the categories of evidence Valora must produce (forensics reports, chain-of-custody logs, internal incident timelines) within X days so the parties can trigger the carve-out?

We appreciate Redwood's prior proposal but need concrete commitments on the types of evidence and timing to satisfy our board. Happy to have a short call if helpful — Andrew and I are available Thu morning PT.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Proposed redline — trade-secret carve-out + evidence buckets

Hannah/Team,

Drafted a tighter clause to circulate to Valora. High level: keep the liability cap in place generally, but exclude from that cap proven misappropriation of "Trade Secrets" where the customer provides (a) a third-party forensic report evidencing unauthorized access and misappropriation, and (b) corroborating system logs or chain-of-custody records.

Key elements in the proposed text (attached as rwi-proposed-forensics-language.docx):
- Definition: "Trade Secret" follows the Uniform Trade Secrets Act definition and is limited to information that (i) has independent economic value from not being generally known and (ii) has reasonable measures to maintain secrecy.
- Trigger: the carve-out applies only where (i) the forensic report (by an agreed-upon independent vendor or mutually acceptable vendor) concludes with a preponderance of evidence that Redwood's systems were the vector for misappropriation, and (ii) Customer provides logs/audit exports within 30 days showing access and exfiltration indicators.
- Forensics: customer may engage a neutral third-party; Redwood reserves the right to engage its own neutral vendor; costs borne equally unless intentional misconduct is found.
- Remedies: if the two-part test is met, damages otherwise limited by the MSA cap do not apply to direct damages for trade-secret theft; consequential damages remain excluded.

Open questions / negotiation levers:
1) "Preponderance" vs "clear and convincing" — Valora may push for lower burdens; higher burden reduces risk for us.
2) Who pays for the independent vendor if results are inconclusive?
3) Timing: 30 days to produce logs is aggressive for some customers; could propose 45 days with a good-faith extension clause.

I tried to minimize open-ended exposure while giving Valora a reasonable path to evidence. If we accept equal-split vendor costs by default, that may be an easier sell. Please review the attached and flag any business/ops issues.

-Vivek
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rwi-proposed-forensics-language.docx

Subject: Re: Proposed redline — trade-secret carve-out + evidence buckets

All,

Operational notes on feasibility:
- Logs & exports: we can provide audit logs, access logs, and S3 object access history. Standard retention is 90 days in hosted, longer in Dedicated — we should call that out. If Valora needs a longer retention SLA, that's a commercial item.
- Timeline: 45 days is more realistic for a complete delivery of chained evidence (we typically need time for internal review, data pulls, and coordination with infra). We can commit to initial logs within 10 business days for triage.
- Forensics vendors: Redwood's security team has a standing panel (vendors A/B/C) we can propose; neutral vendor selection should be by mutual agreement. If Valora insists on their vendor, we need to reserve right to run a parallel analysis.

Commercial impact: accepting an uncapped remediation for proven trade-secret theft creates a material tail risk. Recommend we limit the carve-out to (i) direct actual damages proven and (ii) cap the carve-out at a multiple of the MSA (e.g., 2x) unless intentional misconduct is proven. That gives Valora comfort while bounding our exposure.

Happy to sync with Vivek to put these options into the draft.

-Laura
Director, Procurement & Contracts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA redlines — liability cap / confidentiality carve-out (proposed compromise)

Elena / Andrew — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is Redwood's proposed compromise (rwi-proposed-forensics-language.docx) and a short summary: 

Summary of Redwood proposal (high level):
- Carve-out narrowly limited to proven misappropriation of Trade Secrets (UTA-style definition); not for general confidentiality breaches.
- Two-part evidence trigger: (1) independent forensic report by a mutually agreed vendor concluding misappropriation attributable to Redwood systems, and (2) corroborating system logs/chain-of-custody provided by Customer within 45 days (we can commit to initial triage logs in 10 business days).
- Cost allocation: both parties each pay their vendor by default; if either report demonstrates intentional misconduct by Redwood, Redwood will reimburse the customer's reasonable forensic costs.
- Remedies: direct damages proven by the two-part test fall outside the general cap, but we propose to limit that carve-out to actual direct damages up to 2x the MSA fee for the 12-month period preceding discovery unless intentional misconduct is proven — this is intended to provide Valora meaningful recovery while bounding Redwood's exposure. Consequential damages remain excluded.

Next steps: if this captures a middle ground, we can put the draft into DocuSign for an interim signing amendment and continue fine redlines in parallel. If you'd prefer a call to walk through the language, we are available Mon morning PT.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
